subject: VAT documentation & reverse-charge handling for upcoming invoice
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@octaviasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T08:23:00Z
Subject: VAT documentation & reverse-charge handling for upcoming invoice

Hi Sara —

Hope you’re well. We have your June 30 invoice scheduled (OC-8421) and want to make sure we apply the correct VAT treatment. A few quick asks so Finance can process without delay: 

- Can you confirm Octavia Systems’ legal invoicing entity and billing address that should appear on the invoice?
- Please confirm the VAT ID you want us to use for reverse-charge (if eligible).
- If available, can you attach a copy of the VAT registration certificate (PDF) or a screenshot from the VIES/IRIS portal?

If we receive the VAT ID + certificate, our billing team will mark the invoice as "reverse charge — customer liable" and omit EU VAT on Redwood’s side. Without it, the invoice will be issued with tax and may be subject to reissuance.

Goal: get this resolved by end of day Monday so the invoice goes out cleanly on 6/30.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

Redwood Inference | https://www.redwood.ai

Date: 2026-06-15T14:05:00Z

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the heads up. See details below: 

- Legal entity: Octavia Systems Ltd. (registered office below)
- Billing address: 42 Harcourt St, Dublin 2, D02 XY45, Ireland
- VAT ID: IE 1234567F

I've attached our VAT registration certificate (Octavia_VAT_Certificate_2026.pdf). We are an Irish-registered B2B SaaS provider — reverse charge should apply for services provided to EU vendors when the purchaser is established in another EU Member State, but in this case we asked our tax advisor and they confirm Octavia is VAT-registered in Ireland and eligible for reverse-charge treatment when the customer (Redwood) requests it.

If you need any additional proof (VIES screenshot or company extract), let me know — I can send a PDF from our tax team.

Best,

Sara Hughes

Ben — forwarding Octavia's VAT certificate and entity details (VAT ID IE 1234567F). Can Finance confirm the routing we should use for the 6/30 invoice and whether any additional metadata needs to be recorded on the invoice PDF (e.g., "Reverse charge — Article 44" note, customer VAT ID in the header, billing contact)?

Quick context: Octavia is asking for the invoice to be treated under reverse-charge. They're an Irish entity; their tax advisor confirmed eligibility. We need to: 

- Mark the invoice as reverse-charge (no VAT charged)
- Include the customer VAT ID on the invoice and a short reverse-charge statement
- Upload the VAT certificate to the billing portal / attach it to the DocuSign envelope for audit trail

If there's any reason Finance would still need us to charge VAT, please flag ASAP — Marissa is on-copy to help with account mapping if we need to split entities.

Thanks —

Logan

Thanks Logan — I reviewed the certificate and the IE VAT ID (IE1234567F) validates against our checklists. Actioning the following from Finance: 

- Billing will issue Invoice_20260630_OC-8421.pdf showing net amounts only (no VAT) and include the customer VAT ID in the header.
- We'll add the statement: "Reverse charge — VAT liability shifted to the customer under Article 44 Directive 2006/112/EC (B2B supply of services)."
- I've requested the invoice be attached to the DocuSign envelope with the VAT certificate for our audit folder.
- Please confirm the billing address we print on the invoice (using the Octavia address Sara provided). If you prefer a different invoicing entity or PO reference, tell us now — otherwise we'll proceed as above.

Notes for ops: Marissa, please tag the account in Billing Portal as "eu-b2b-reverse-charge" and upload Octavia_VAT_Certificate_2026.pdf to the account documents. HubSpot deal HS-58329 should be updated with the VAT ID and the reverse-charge flag.
